pages.title: Prying Eyes wiki
pages.summary: The guide to Prying Eyes: its two ways to play, its places, enemies, objects and systems, the production suite and the history, with a picture and links for every page.

pages.title: Decima
pages.summary: Decima (tithe) is a blessing of the altar: the points you earn from kills are 25% higher for the next expedition.

pages.title: Furia
pages.summary: Furia (fury) is a blessing of the altar: +20% damage for the next expedition.

pages.title: Grazia
pages.summary: Grazia (grace) is a blessing of the altar: +30 maximum health for the next expedition.

pages.title: Porte d'oro
pages.summary: Porte d'oro (golden doors) is a blessing of the altar: the paid doors cost 30% less for the next expedition.

pages.title: Provvidenza
pages.summary: Provvidenza (providence) is a blessing of the altar: the power-ups drop twice as often for the next expedition.

pages.title: Raccolto
pages.summary: Raccolto (harvest) is a blessing of the altar: the resources you gather are multiplied by 1.5 for the next expedition.

pages.title: Il Guardaroba del Conte (branch IV)
pages.summary: The fourth branch, the Count's wardrobe: wardrobes, vampires, scissors and lava terraces, opened by the Count's gate and led by the Conte.

pages.title: L'Ossario (branch I)
pages.summary: The first branch of the catacombs, open from the start: hotel and church floors, with the Cardinale on the third level.

pages.title: Il Sanatorio (branch III)
pages.summary: The third branch, a sanatorium: wards, cells, an operating room and linoleum under flickering tubes; opened by the sanatorium gate, with the Primario as its boss.

pages.title: Il Teatro sepolto (branch II)
pages.summary: The second branch, a buried theatre: an auditorium, a stage and dressing rooms; opened by the theatre gate, with the Direttore as its boss.

pages.title: The camp
pages.summary: A camp is a fire ringed with stones, with one to three tents whose doors face it and a pile of supplies; by day the fire is out, at night it burns.

pages.title: The campfire
pages.summary: A campfire is the fire of a camp at night: a flickering light, smoke and sparks, and a crackle heard within 34 m; the four nearest fires within 130 m light the sand.

pages.title: Catalogue
pages.summary: Every page of the wiki by class and kind, with its mode and its one-line summary, generated from the pages by tools/wiki_site.py.

pages.title: The glass eye
pages.summary: The glass eye is one of three hidden on every catacomb floor: take all three and the weapon in your hand is consecrated for free, and you get 1,000 points.

pages.title: Concept map
pages.summary: How the main concepts of the game and of the project connect, as a diagram: each concept with its page, and each relation with its label.

pages.title: The lizard
pages.summary: The lizard lives on the desert sand by day and runs away when you come within 6.5 m; it hurts nobody.

pages.title: The scarab
pages.summary: The scarab is a beetle of the desert sand: by day it lives on the sand and runs away when you come within 6.5 m; it hurts nobody.

pages.title: The scorpion
pages.summary: The scorpion lives on the desert sand by day and is the shyest of the ground animals: it runs away when you come within 3.8 m. It hurts nobody.

pages.title: The vulture
pages.summary: The vulture is a bird of the desert that circles over the ruins and the towers, in flocks of up to five within 700 m; by day one caws from the flock nearest to you, and at night the bats take its place.

pages.title: The candle cycle
pages.summary: The legacy cycle of the tower, still there with the -candles flag; each floor has candles to light, and lighting them calls enemies, so stealth decides the run.

pages.title: Day and night
pages.summary: In the desert a day lasts twenty minutes, about twelve of daylight and eight of night; the hour sets the light, the fog and the enemies, which rest by day and wake at night.

pages.title: Sandstorm
pages.summary: About one day in two the desert has a sandstorm between 08:00 and 22:00 that lasts 75 to 160 seconds of play; the fog thickens, the sun weakens and the animals take shelter.

pages.title: The wave cycle
pages.summary: The default cycle of the tower: no candles and no stealth, waves that start on their own, areas bought with points, a procession of lights every fifth wave and a Cardinale every eighth.

pages.title: Area door (paid door)
pages.summary: A door you open with points: the first area costs 500, each further one 250 more per step from the start, up to 1500; it opens for everyone for the rest of the floor.

pages.title: The abbot
pages.summary: The abbot is the monk made larger and dressed in black and gold, with 320 hit points and a heavier charge and lunge; the eighth-wave Cardinale is built on its body.

pages.title: The Appestato
pages.summary: The Appestato is a slow, plague-bearing monk with 230 hit points that bursts when it reaches you and when it dies, leaving a toxic cloud behind.

pages.title: The Cardinale
pages.summary: The Cardinale is the boss of every eighth wave and of the first branch, the Ossario: a crimson robe, a mitre and a gold halo, a fire ring, a five-bolt fan, and hit points that grow with the players and the waves.

pages.title: The Conte
pages.summary: The Conte is the Cardinale's body in the Guardaroba: the boss of the fourth branch, tinted toward crimson, with the Cardinale's hit points and attacks, and a trophy of gems.

pages.title: The Direttore
pages.summary: The Direttore is the theatre's conductor and the boss of the second branch: 2.4 m tall with a top hat and a tuning fork, 330 hit points, a charge telegraphed for 1.2 seconds and a fan of darts.

pages.title: The Flagellante
pages.summary: The Flagellante is a monk in a red robe that runs at you and leaps from a few metres away, with 95 hit points and a strike when it lands.

pages.title: The flying eye
pages.summary: The flying eye (Occhio) is an 80-hit-point eye that flies instead of walking; in the desert it comes out only at night, and by day a monk takes its place.

pages.title: The Infermiere
pages.summary: The Infermiere is the sanatorium's nurse: a stained gown with a red cross and a drip stand, 190 hit points, and a sedative needle that slows you to 55% for 2.8 seconds.

pages.title: The Maschera
pages.summary: The Maschera is the theatre's usher: a faded harlequin with a porcelain mask, 150 hit points, fast and melee only, whose whistle alarms the others at first sight.

pages.title: The Medusa
pages.summary: The Medusa is the flying jellyfish of the procedural floors: 140 hit points, a speed of 1.9, a bell lit green from inside, and a lunge with a jet of mucus. It does not appear in the desert.

pages.title: The monk
pages.summary: The monk is the common enemy of both modes, with 200 hit points and a long robe; most other enemies are built on its body, and in the desert it is the most frequent walker.

pages.title: The Portachiavi
pages.summary: The Portachiavi is the reception's key cabinet turned into a walking reliquary: tarnished brass, four articulated keys, a bell that warns before its blow, and a glowing lock as its weak point.

pages.title: The Primario
pages.summary: The Primario is the sanatorium's chief physician and the boss of the third branch: as large as an abbot, with 360 hit points, and a call that brings two nurses.

pages.title: The lord of the place
pages.summary: The lord of the place is the boss of a desert tower or catacomb: one of the four branch bosses, chosen by the place, waiting in the hall at the top of a tower or at the bottom of a catacomb.

pages.title: The Statua
pages.summary: The Statua is a stone monk that moves only when nobody looks at it: 720 hit points, a run at 5.2 m/s when unseen, and bullets that do 40% of their damage.

pages.title: The Veglia
pages.summary: The Veglia is a candle hung in a torn votive veil: fragile and fast, with 60 hit points and two embers in its wax face as its weak point, and the enemy of the processions of lights.

pages.title: Low passage
pages.summary: A low opening in a wall that you crawl through, holding C or Ctrl: it leads into the secret room and into the hidden walls of the floor.

pages.title: Portcullis (the iron gate)
pages.summary: The iron portcullis that closes the stone landing of a catacomb level: it rises when the way is open, and a torch and a lantern light the arch.

pages.title: Shutter (steel and round)
pages.summary: The steel shutter of the Tower: it closes the lifts of the wave-cycle floors until three waves are cleared, and it seals a candle round in the candle cycle.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: The words of the game and of the project, with the game's Italian names where it has them, each defined in a line and linked to the page that explains it.

pages.title: Grade I (Ordinary)
pages.summary: Grade I, Ordinary, in grey: three weapons, the starting pistol, the Vigilia and the Tarantola; the only grade the sand gives for free.

pages.title: Grade II (Choice)
pages.summary: Grade II, Choice, in green: ten weapons, from the revolver and the SMGs to the shotguns; the sacristy's rack gives three of them for free.

pages.title: Grade III (Rare)
pages.summary: Grade III, Rare, in blue: seven weapons, from the bullpups and the precision rifle to the sacred flamethrower; the forge gives one of the rack's weapons this grade.

pages.title: Grade IV (Epic)
pages.summary: Grade IV, Epic, in purple: six weapons, the magnum, the battle rifle, the sniper rifle, the drum shotgun, the light machine gun and the alien launcher.

pages.title: Grade V (Relic)
pages.summary: Grade V, Relic, in gold: the anti-materiel rifle that pierces five enemies and the eye-rifle with its amber beam; the rarest grade.

pages.title: The Book of the Arsenal
pages.summary: The Book of the Arsenal is the 19-node magic book for the weapons: twelve outer nodes that work on every weapon, six inner nodes that are seals traced on the weapon, and the supreme node, Arma Maledetta.

pages.title: The Book of Witchcraft
pages.summary: The Book of Witchcraft is a 19-node magic book: twelve outer nodes that improve the left hand, six inner nodes that are its spells, and the supreme node, Essenza Maledetta.

pages.title: Broken lamps
pages.summary: Electric lamps of the standard floors break with one shot; their light leaves the pool, their flicker stops, their bulbs go dark, and in a fight the room really gets darker.

pages.title: Falling chandeliers
pages.summary: Chandeliers are iron crowns hung over the standard floors; 60 points of damage bring one down, its fall kills the enemies beneath it, and it stays behind as a navmesh obstacle.

pages.title: Holy-oil barrels
pages.summary: Holy-oil barrels are wooden casks with a red cross that explode after two shots or a nearby blast, with a fireball of 520 damage and a chain reaction to every barrel within 4.5 m.

pages.title: The butte
pages.summary: A butte is a lone rock of layered stone, 28 to 95 m tall and 60 to 130 m long, with a flat top and a skirt of rubble; at most one stands in each 900 m square.

pages.title: The landmark tower
pages.summary: The landmark tower is a tower of at least seven floors 350 m from the cathedral, always in the same place, with a banner on its roof, and a mark a player steers to on the horizon.

pages.title: The obelisk
pages.summary: An obelisk is a tall stone pillar of 8 to 14 m that stands on the open sand of the holy land and shows from afar.

pages.title: The welcome chapel
pages.summary: The welcome chapel is a ruined chapel 100 m from the cathedral, always in the same place: the first landmark a player walks to from the churchyard.

pages.title: The well
pages.summary: A well is a round hole in the sand that shows from afar; the stair of a catacomb goes down through one of them, under a mausoleum.

pages.title: The windmill
pages.summary: A windmill is a ruined mill of the hamlets whose sails turn with the wind, which the desert page says turns the windmills and is heard across the sand.

pages.title: The boss level
pages.summary: The third level of a branch: after three waves the next opens with the branch's boss and half its usual escort; clearing it opens the gate.

pages.title: The first level of a branch
pages.summary: The first level of every branch: the arrival through its gate, the poor box, the remains of an earlier death, and floors that play like the Tower's.

pages.title: The desert
pages.summary: The open world of sand: one seed, six regions, towers and catacombs on the sand, a day of twenty minutes, sandstorms, a motorbike and four bosses; no waves, no stealth, nothing saved.

pages.title: Standard mode
pages.summary: The game of the cathedral: a base you rebuild, the catacombs under it with four branches and their bosses, and the waves and trials that come at the top.

pages.title: Production Economy
pages.summary: The engine-free rules of the cathedral's money: a resource ledger, one-off constructions, market exchanges, weighted loot and the rules of what you keep when you come back.

pages.title: Production Layout
pages.summary: Deterministic district layouts with no Unity and no game dependency: the same seed gives the same plan, and an independent project proves that the package works outside the game.

pages.title: Production Saves
pages.summary: Engine-independent save documents: a JSON tree, versioned formats with a chain of migrations that upgrades old saves one step at a time, and a file store with atomic writes, backups and quarantine.

pages.title: Production Survival
pages.summary: Engine-independent rules for the waves of the wave cycle: the budget of enemies per wave, the pace of their spawns and the limit on how many are alive at once.

pages.title: Production Weapons
pages.summary: Engine-independent data and rules of a weapon: its record, the rules of a catalogue, ammunition, the transitions of a reload and the cadence of the shots, with no engine and no game dependency.

pages.title: Doppio colpo
pages.summary: Doppio colpo (double tap) is a perk that raises the fire rate by 33%, sold as a magic book in the library.

pages.title: Mani svelte
pages.summary: Mani svelte (quick hands) is a perk that reloads 40% faster; the Cappella delle Mani work starts every expedition with it.

pages.title: Occhio della Torre
pages.summary: Occhio della Torre (eye of the tower) is a perk whose ping shows enemies through walls and raises headshot damage by 25%.

pages.title: Passi di cenere
pages.summary: Passi di cenere (ash steps) is a perk that makes your footsteps heard 40% less.

pages.title: Pelle di pietra
pages.summary: Pelle di pietra (stone skin) is a perk: +50% health. Its magic book is in the library, and the Cappella della Pietra work starts every expedition with it.

pages.title: Rinascita
pages.summary: Rinascita (rebirth) is a perk that lets you rise once per floor, on the spot, after three seconds of respite instead of dying; the apothecary's Cero votivo starts an expedition with it.

pages.title: Sete di sangue
pages.summary: Sete di sangue (blood thirst) is a perk that heals 25 points for every knife kill and 40 for every takedown.

pages.title: Velo
pages.summary: Velo (veil) is a perk that makes you seen 30% less, and with H it makes you invisible for five seconds; it is not offered in the wave cycle.

pages.title: Ammunition crate
pages.summary: The ammunition crate is a desert find that refills the reserve of each weapon you carry by half of its maximum.

pages.title: Essence crystal
pages.summary: The essence crystal is a desert find that gives 30 essence, the resource of the left hand that pays for spells and seals.

pages.title: Medikit
pages.summary: The medikit is a desert find, a white box with a red cross, that restores 50 health when you walk up to it.

pages.title: Points (gold coins)
pages.summary: Gold coins are the desert's points pickup; walk up to one and its value goes to your score, doubled while an Offerta runs.

pages.title: Blender models
pages.summary: The Blender scripts that model the weapons, the hotel furniture, the characters, the monk and the other figures of the game, and bake them for Unity; they live in modelli/.

pages.title: Check suite
pages.summary: The boundary guard of the reusable suite and of the documentation: it fails when a package names the game, when the engine names a tool, or when a link or a path breaks.

pages.title: CI gate
pages.summary: The workflow on GitHub that runs the boundary check, the Python tests and every .NET lab the studio lists on every push to preview and every pull request against it.

pages.title: Labs
pages.summary: The engine-free .NET labs that run the rules of the packages and of the game's pure code without the editor, listed by the studio's suites command and run by its test command.

pages.title: Release
pages.summary: How a release of the game is prepared: checks, a distribution build, a scan for the paths of one machine, a zip with its checksum and a smoke test. It publishes nothing.

pages.title: Ship
pages.summary: The script that commits, builds, smoke-tests, pushes and refreshes the game the maintainer plays, in one run that an agent starts detached and waits for.

pages.title: Studio engine
pages.summary: The project-agnostic production engine: jobs with reports, a lock per project, a source guard, owned processes and a persistent queue, in standard-library Python.

pages.title: Wiki generator
pages.summary: The generator that turns the Markdown pages of wiki/ into the catalogue, the concept map, the graph file and the static site, and fails on any broken link, missing image or stale file.

pages.title: The chapel (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert chapel is a small church-like place marked with a cross on the minimap, found most often in the holy land; the welcome chapel, 100 m from the cathedral, is always one.

pages.title: The church (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert church is the largest kind of church-like place of the holy land, marked with a cross on the minimap, with a nave and a yard that holds steles, cairns and a broken column.

pages.title: The complex (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert complex is a large place made of many rooms of several kinds, shown here in ruin with about twenty-four rooms; the desert page names it among the eight kinds of place and gives no more detail.

pages.title: The hotel (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert hotel is a large place of the dead town, built from the rooms of the hotel of the floors, whole or falling apart, with a roof, a yard of props and guards.

pages.title: The house (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert house is a small place of a few rooms, whole, ruined, split or collapsing, that stands on the sand of the hamlets; it has two to four props in its yard and its own guards.

pages.title: The inn (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert inn is a small hostelry of the hamlets, found here in ruin, built from the rooms of the floors and given a yard of props and guards like the other places.

pages.title: The sanatorium (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert sanatorium is a place of the dead town built from the wards of the sanatorium of the floors, whole or falling apart; like the theatre, it has enemies of its own.

pages.title: The theatre (desert place)
pages.summary: A desert theatre is a place of the dead town built from the rooms of the theatre of the floors, whole or falling apart; the desert gives theatres enemies of their own.

pages.title: Campana
pages.summary: Campana (bell) is a power-up that kills everyone in the round and within 22 metres and pays 400 points, but its toll is heard across the whole floor and the survivors come looking for you.

pages.title: Offerta
pages.summary: Offerta (offering) is a power-up that doubles every gain of points for 30 seconds; in co-op and split screen it works for everyone.

pages.title: Reliquiario
pages.summary: The Reliquiario is a power-up that fills the magazines and reserves of both weapons to the maximum; a procession always leaves one where its last Veglia died.

pages.title: Sguardo
pages.summary: Sguardo (gaze) is a power-up that makes every shot kill for 30 seconds, except the bell's blast.

pages.title: City prototype
pages.summary: The station district: a playable base built as its own scene from a recipe, with buildings to visit, stalls on the road and a wave hall, checked by its own lab and by the production suite.

pages.title: Earlier versions
pages.summary: The three versions before the Unity game: a Three.js prototype that runs in the browser, an Unreal Engine 5 prototype with a playable first-person room, and the first Unity hall that stays in the project outside the build.

pages.title: Quality audit
pages.summary: The review of the complete version, run in dated passes from 12 November 2026: weapons, movement, co-op, hordes, rooms, HUD and lighting, each with its evidence and its open work.

pages.title: The trailer
pages.summary: The trailer is filmed from the game itself: a recorder inside the player follows a shot list, and Python scripts cut, caption and score the clips, so the trailer can be made again from data.

pages.title: The Unity game
pages.summary: Prying Eyes itself: a Unity 6000.6.7f1 project with one playable scene, the cathedral and the floors, the two modes, the builds the maintainer plays and the packages it uses.

pages.title: Unreal prototype
pages.summary: A feasibility test, not a port: one generated room of the Unity game rebuilt in Unreal Engine 5.8 from the command line, with no Blueprints, and photographed in both engines to compare the look and the frame times.

pages.title: Survival redesign
pages.summary: The redesign toward the pace of Call of Duty Zombies: candles and stealth out, the waves in, areas bought with points and faster enemies, carried through in seventeen passes that the history keeps.

pages.title: The wardrobe
pages.summary: The wardrobe (arr-armadio) is a two-door cabinet with a moulded cornice, raised panels and brass hinges; its left door stands ajar on a red velvet lining with three dark coats hanging inside.

pages.title: The bedside table
pages.summary: The bedside table (arr-comodino) is a small table with a moulded top, four turned legs, a drawer and a panelled door, placed beside the beds of the hotel's bedrooms and in the sanatorium's wards.

pages.title: The range cooker
pages.summary: The range cooker (arr-fornello) is a steel range with six burners, six control knobs, a clock and a hood; the hotel kitchen lines its far wall with them, and the wardrobe's forge hangs one on a wall.

pages.title: The floor lamp
pages.summary: The floor lamp (arr-lampada) is a brass lamp with a rope-twist stem, a bulb in a wire harp and a 24-pleat shade; it stands in hotel, sanatorium and theatre rooms, and a shot can break its bulb.

pages.title: The warehouse shelf
pages.summary: The warehouse shelf (arr-scaffale) is a steel-upright shelf of five wooden shelves loaded with boxes, jars, tins, linen and books, placed along walls and as cover in the hotel, sanatorium, theatre and wardrobe kits.

pages.title: The writing desk
pages.summary: The writing desk (arr-scrivania) is a desk with a leather writing surface edged in brass wire and a pedestal of three drawers, with an inkwell, a sheet of paper, books and a candlestick on top.

pages.title: The dining chair
pages.summary: The dining chair (arr-sedia) is a turned-leg chair with a curved backrest and an upholstered seat, placed beside restaurant tables, in ballroom rows, at bedroom desks and in the sanatorium and theatre kits.

pages.title: The steel work table
pages.summary: The steel work table (arr-tavolo-acciaio) is a workbench with a rolled-edge top, a drawer with a bar handle and a lower shelf, placed in a row across the hotel's kitchen and in the sanatorium's rooms.

pages.title: The dining table
pages.summary: The dining table (arr-tavolo) is a square table under a long draped cloth, with a candlestick and two place settings, placed in restaurants, theatre rooms and the cathedral's sacristy.

pages.title: The stone altar
pages.summary: The stone altar (chi-altare) is an ashlar altar with five pointed arches, a golden Eye in a medallion and a monstrance; the church kit places it in presbyteries and chapels, the cathedral's choir and the annexes.

pages.title: The baptismal font
pages.summary: The baptismal font (chi-fonte) is an octagonal stone font with black water and a pyramidal oak lid propped open at 30 degrees; the cathedral's hub shows it once its work is built, and rotundas, church narthexes, the winter garden and the garden annex place it too.

pages.title: The prie-dieu
pages.summary: The prie-dieu (chi-inginocchiatoio) is a praying desk with a padded kneeler, a back with a pointed arch and a brass cross, and a sloped lectern with an open book; it stands in church chapels and beside the cathedral's chapel works.

pages.title: The church pew
pages.summary: The church pew (chi-panca) is a long bench with Gothic arches and a hymn rack; it is the most placed of the church props, filling naves, rotundas, the garden annex and the wardrobe's rooms.

pages.title: The stone sarcophagus
pages.summary: The stone sarcophagus (chi-sarcofago) is a moulded stone tomb with a blind arcade along each side and a lid slid aside to show the bones; it has the most triangles at level 0 of the sixteen props.

pages.title: The choir stall
pages.summary: The choir stall (chi-stallo) is an oak seat for three with four standards cut as single plates, round poppyheads and a canopy of 24 pointed arches; the church kit places them along both sides of the presbytery.

pages.title: The hooded monk statue
pages.summary: The hooded monk statue (chi-statua) is a stone monk on a plinth with a brass plate and a single golden eye in its hood; it stands in church rooms, in the cathedral's chapel works and in the garden annex.

pages.title: The badlands (region)
pages.summary: The badlands are the desert region of red ground, many mesas, towers and catacombs, red rocks and layered slabs; buttes are most common here, and the ground rises most.

pages.title: The dead town (region)
pages.summary: The dead town is the desert region of ash-grey ground with hotels, theatres and sanatoria falling apart, wagons and bones; only 16% of its places are whole.

pages.title: The dunes (region)
pages.summary: The dunes are the desert region of the highest transverse dunes: crests across the wind, 120 to 230 m apart, 9 m high near the cathedral and 18 m far out.

pages.title: The hamlets (region)
pages.summary: The hamlets are the desert region of dry earth with many small houses, inns, wells and windmills; the cathedral always stands in it, and it has the most places of any region.

pages.title: The holy land (region)
pages.summary: The holy land is the desert region of pale chalk with chapels, churches, columns, steles and obelisks, and it has catacombs among its places.

pages.title: The salt flats (region)
pages.summary: The salt flats are the desert region of white, flat and almost empty ground, with bones and white rocks, a film of water over a third of its interior, and almost no dunes.

pages.title: Acciaio
pages.summary: Acciaio (steel) is a common resource: keys, needles and chains, used for the gates, the forge and the bells, and dropped by abbots, statues and the Portachiavi.

pages.title: Brace
pages.summary: Brace (embers) is a rare resource: the fire left in the Veglie, which lights the forge and the organ pipes and is needed by the Cappella delle Mani.

pages.title: Cristalli d'oscurità
pages.summary: Cristalli d'oscurità (darkness crystals) is the boss resource of the second branch, steeped in the dark of the buried theatre and carried by the Direttore; they open the Cancello del Sanatorio.

pages.title: Cristalli di fede
pages.summary: Cristalli di fede (faith crystals) is the boss resource of the third branch: the prayers of the sick, crystallised, kept by the Primario; they open the Cancello del Conte.

pages.title: Cuori
pages.summary: Cuori (hearts) is a rare resource: hearts that still beat, which the altars want; abbots and chief physicians drop them.

pages.title: Gemme
pages.summary: Gemme (gems) is the boss resource of the fourth branch, the treasure of the Conte at the bottom of the Guardaroba; they build the Vetrata del Conte.

pages.title: Legno
pages.summary: Legno (wood) is a common resource: staves, rosaries and pew splinters, used for the beams, the organ and the confessionals.

pages.title: Ossa
pages.summary: Ossa (bones) is the commonest resource: the bones of friars and pilgrims, the lime of the vaults, dropped by monks and Veglie and used by the largest works.

pages.title: Reliquie
pages.summary: Reliquie (relics) is the boss resource of the first branch: the relics of the Cardinale, lord of the Ossario, which open the Cancello del Teatro and build two windows.

pages.title: Sangue
pages.summary: Sangue (blood) is a rare resource in phials: the water of the font and the ink of the vows, dropped by flying things and nurses, and needed by the baptismal font and the window of the Conte.

pages.title: Arena (Candela)
pages.summary: The room with a fire-coloured door frame and a candle: in the candle cycle, lighting the candle seals the room and starts a round; in the wave cycle the arena is decoration.

pages.title: Boss room (Boss)
pages.summary: The room with a crimson door frame, where the exit lift stands and its guardian waits: an abbot, or the themed boss, with twice or two and a half times the hit points.

pages.title: Guard room (Guardia)
pages.summary: A room with a steel door frame where one or two guards patrol until they notice you; in the candle cycle that is a matter of stealth.

pages.title: Library room (Biblioteca)
pages.summary: The room with a violet door frame and three lecterns: the perk books, bought one at a time with points, from 2000 to 4000 for the four slots.

pages.title: Secret room (Segreta)
pages.summary: The room with a turquoise door frame, entered only through a low passage: enemies do not reach it, and it holds the Consacrazione altar; the candle cycle only.

pages.title: Shop room (Negozio)
pages.summary: The room with a gold door frame: two weapons on the wall and the Scrigno, the mystery chest that costs 950 points.

pages.title: Start room (Partenza)
pages.summary: The room where a floor begins, with a green door frame: the arrival lift and a modest weapon on the wall.

pages.title: Arma Maledetta
pages.summary: Arma Maledetta (cursed weapon) is the top seal of the Book of the Arsenal: for 15 seconds the weapon does double damage with all six seals at once and has infinite ammunition; it costs 60 essence and has a 90-second cooldown.

pages.title: Corrosivo
pages.summary: Corrosivo (corrosive) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: for five seconds everything does 30% more damage to the enemy, who also takes 4 damage a second, for 40 essence.

pages.title: Danni Critici
pages.summary: Danni Critici (critical damage) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: one hit in four is critical and does two and a half times the damage; it lasts 45 seconds for 40 essence.

pages.title: Elettrificato
pages.summary: Elettrificato (electrified) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: each hit stuns for 0.4 seconds and arcs to two neighbours at 40% of the damage, for 40 essence.

pages.title: Gelido
pages.summary: Gelido (icy) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: each hit slows the target, and four hits freeze it for two seconds, for 40 essence.

pages.title: Incendiario
pages.summary: Incendiario (incendiary) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: the weapon burns its target for 10 damage a second over four seconds, for 40 essence.

pages.title: Sanguinamento
pages.summary: Sanguinamento (bleeding) is a seal of the Book of the Arsenal: each hit opens a bleed of 8 damage a second, up to three stacks, for 40 essence.

pages.title: Catena del Fulmine
pages.summary: Catena del Fulmine is the lightning spell of the Book of Witchcraft: 90 damage to the target in sight, then a chain that jumps to four more enemies within 6 m at 70% each, for 35 essence.

pages.title: Essenza Maledetta
pages.summary: Essenza Maledetta (cursed essence) is the supreme spell of the Book of Witchcraft: for 12 seconds, spells cost nothing and come back faster, damage is up 60%, and enemies close by burn; it costs 60 essence.

pages.title: Fiamma Sacrilega
pages.summary: Fiamma Sacrilega is the first spell of the Book of Witchcraft: a fireball for 30 essence, with 140 damage at its centre, falling to 36% at 3.5 m, and four seconds of burning.

pages.title: Morsa di Gelo
pages.summary: Morsa di Gelo is the frost spell of the Book of Witchcraft: a 7 m cone of 60 damage and a slow, and a second hit freezes the enemy for 2.5 seconds; it costs 30 essence.

pages.title: Onda del Dodecaedro
pages.summary: Onda del Dodecaedro is the wave spell of the Book of Witchcraft: a 200-degree wave of 70 damage that throws enemies back and stuns them for half a second, for 35 essence.

pages.title: Passo d'Ombra
pages.summary: Passo d'Ombra is the shadow step of the Book of Witchcraft: a teleport up to 8 m ahead that stops before walls, for 30 essence.

pages.title: Sigillo di Sangue
pages.summary: Sigillo di Sangue is the drain spell of the Book of Witchcraft: it drains the target in sight for 1.5 seconds, healing you by half of it, and gives 20 essence if it kills; it costs 25 essence.

pages.title: The catacomb (desert stack)
pages.summary: A desert catacomb is a mausoleum whose stair goes down through a well in the sand to three to five levels, each 5.4 m below the one above, with its boss in the bottom hall.

pages.title: The tower (desert stack)
pages.summary: A desert tower is a stack of 7 to 14 floors, up to 76 m tall, built as an outside as well as a set of rooms, with corner turrets and banners on top and its boss in the hall of the top floor.

pages.title: Il banco dell'armaiolo
pages.summary: The armourer's counter: a mine, a carillon and a letter of credit, two of each per return; the letter gives 500 points at the start.

pages.title: Il carro dell'ossaio
pages.summary: The bone cart: lots of ten bones, wood or steel, bought for 25, 30 or 40 oboli and sold back for 8, 10 or 12; three lots of each per return.

pages.title: La bottega della speziale
pages.summary: The apothecary stall of the square: holy water, a votive candle, and a map of the catacomb level; its stock refills on every return.

pages.title: La tenda del cerusico
pages.summary: The surgeon's tent: one rare resource at a time, Brace, Cuori or Sangue, bought for 30 to 40 oboli and sold back for 9 to 12; two per return.

pages.title: Standard vs desert
pages.summary: What differs between the standard mode and the desert, topic by topic and page by page, with one line for each page and the page that says more.

pages.title: The Cacciatrice
pages.summary: The Cacciatrice is the fourth survivor: strong-legged, with auburn hair in a long braid under a dark cap, an oxblood jacket, olive trousers and an amber scarf.

pages.title: The Custode
pages.summary: The Custode is the first of the four survivors: stocky, with grey hair and a moustache, an olive canvas jacket, a red wool scarf and a tweed cap.

pages.title: The Dottoressa
pages.summary: The Dottoressa is the second survivor: slight, with a brown bob that covers the ears, a cream coat, charcoal trousers and a teal scarf.

pages.title: The Reporter
pages.summary: The Reporter is the third survivor: fair, with short dark-blond hair and a fringe swept to the side, a mustard jacket, blue trousers and a grey scarf.

pages.title: Annexes
pages.summary: Annexes are hidden rooms of the tower floors in the wave cycle, a tower, a crypt, a garden and a secret book room, each behind its own gate; the desert has none.

pages.title: Blessings
pages.summary: After every return from the catacombs the altar offers three of six blessings, and the one you light before a descent lasts for the whole descent.

pages.title: Online co-op
pages.summary: Up to four players share one tower or desert over the internet; the host runs the enemies and the rules, and each player keeps their own points, weapons, perks and store.

pages.title: Controller
pages.summary: Only XInput pads are read, Xbox 360, One and Series; the game adopts the first pad that presses a button, and its hints switch to the pad's names while it is in use.

pages.title: Display and menu
pages.summary: The main menu is a hotel register with an engraved eye; its settings have five tabs, Schermo, Immagine, Audio, Comandi and Gioco, each row is saved at once, and F3 shows the frame counter.

pages.title: Downed and revive
pages.summary: At zero health you go down and crawl instead of dying; a teammate within reach revives you, you can get up yourself once per floor, and otherwise you bleed out after 30 seconds.

pages.title: Floor power
pages.summary: In the wave cycle every floor starts on emergency lighting; pulling the lever of the electrical panel brings the power back, and until then the perk books, the door traps and the altar refuse to work.

pages.title: The knife
pages.summary: The knife, called Misericordia, is the G key; its stab is loud, while in the candle cycle a takedown from behind is silent and pays 130 points.

pages.title: Medals
pages.summary: Medals are instant feats such as chains of kills, headshots in a row and a kill at low health; each pays a few points, plays a chime and is counted on the Tab scoreboard.

pages.title: Menu music
pages.summary: The main menu plays a waltz for music box and organ in D minor, generated by the game at start-up, and four short tones for its buttons; no audio file is shipped.

pages.title: Minimap and way home
pages.summary: In the desert, N shows a 512 m chart drawn north up, with you, your companions, the awake enemies within 90 m and your parked bike; from 90 m out a golden arrow points back to the cathedral.

pages.title: Perks
pages.summary: Perks are eight magic books that change how you play while you hold them; you hold up to four, bought at a library for 2,000 to 4,000 points, and dying takes the last one.

pages.title: Points and oboli
pages.summary: Points are the score you spend on doors, perks, weapons and power-ups; in the catacombs the points you keep climb back alive as oboli, the coin of the market.

pages.title: The satchel
pages.summary: In the catacombs enemies drop resources that you pull into the satchel by walking close; coming back up banks it in the cathedral's store, and dying leaves the remains on the first level of the branch.

pages.title: Characters and saves
pages.summary: A character is a name with one of the four survivors' looks; it keeps its experience, its cathedral and its history, and an expedition can be suspended and resumed.

pages.title: Split screen
pages.summary: Two to four people play one PC in the same game, each with a view, a HUD, a body, weapons, points and a controller, over the game window or over several monitors.

pages.title: Stealth
pages.summary: Stealth is the rule set of the candle cycle, where monks, abbots and eyes patrol and search, the lights dim as you go down, and a knife takedown from behind is silent.

pages.title: Third-person view
pages.summary: The Prospettiva setting puts the camera behind your survivor's shoulder and brings it closer while aiming or passing an obstacle.

pages.title: The carillon
pages.summary: The carillon is a music box thrown with 4: it plays a lullaby that lures every enemy within 35 m for seven seconds, then explodes for 650 damage at its centre.

pages.title: Holy water
pages.summary: Holy water is a flask thrown with Z: two at the start, up to four, and a blue-white burst of 420 damage at its centre after a two-second fuse.

pages.title: The fire door trap
pages.summary: The fire door trap is a wall of flame at a paid door, switched on by a lever for 20 seconds for 1000 points; it kills every ordinary enemy that crosses the threshold, then recharges for 40 seconds.

pages.title: The lightning door trap
pages.summary: The lightning door trap is the blue-arc twin of the fire trap: the same lever, 1000 points for 20 seconds and 40 seconds of recharge, killing every ordinary enemy that crosses the threshold.

pages.title: The reliquary mine
pages.summary: The reliquary mine (key 5) is a brass disc with a red glass dome that a walking enemy sets off within 1.7 m, for up to 520 damage; a player never sets it off and is never hurt by it.

pages.title: Trial: Coltello
pages.summary: The knife trial of a wave, drawn from the third wave on: three plus a quarter of the wave number, at most 6, knife kills before the wave ends.

pages.title: Trial: Esplosivi
pages.summary: The explosives trial of a wave: four plus a third of the wave number, at most 10, kills by explosions, flasks, traps and bursts before the wave ends.

pages.title: Trial: Furia
pages.summary: The fury trial of a wave: eight plus a third of the wave number, at most 14, kills within 15 seconds; when the window runs out the count restarts.

pages.title: Trial: Intatto
pages.summary: The untouched trial of a wave: forty seconds in a row without taking a hit before the wave ends; a hit starts the count again.

pages.title: Trial: Testa
pages.summary: The headshot trial of a wave: six plus half the wave number, at most 14, headshot kills before the wave ends; it pays points and maybe a power-up.

pages.title: The motorbike
pages.summary: The motorbike is the desert's vehicle: one for each player at the foot of the cathedral stair, a dark red arcade bike with a top speed of 83 km/h, a turbo, tyre tracks in the sand, and a rifle fired from the saddle.

pages.title: ALTARE-50
pages.summary: Grade V anti-materiel rifle: 420 damage that pierces five enemies, a magazine of 5 and a 10x scope; the heaviest weapon of the game.

pages.title: APOCALISSE-12
pages.summary: Grade IV automatic drum shotgun: eight pellets of 11 damage at 300 rounds a minute, a magazine of 20 and a holographic sight.

pages.title: AR-9 MALLEUS
pages.summary: Grade II assault rifle: 30 damage at 700 rounds a minute on automatic or semi-automatic, a magazine of 30 and a red dot.

pages.title: ARCANGELO-47
pages.summary: Grade III assault rifle: 42 damage at 600 rounds a minute on automatic or semi-automatic, a magazine of 30 and tangent iron sights.

pages.title: BORDONE
pages.summary: Grade III bullpup PDW: 23 damage at 900 rounds a minute, a magazine of 50 in the top, and a ring sight.

pages.title: BREACHER-12
pages.summary: Grade II pump shotgun: eight pellets of 15 damage each, a tube of 8 rounds, and a ghost-ring sight.

pages.title: CAMPANA-249
pages.summary: Grade IV light machine gun: 40 damage at 780 rounds a minute, a belt of 100 rounds and a 3x ACOG.

pages.title: CAPPELLANO
pages.summary: Grade II double-barrel shotgun: two barrels of 10 pellets of 14 damage each, two shots in the magazine, broken open to reload.

pages.title: CARDINALE .357
pages.summary: Grade II revolver: 70 damage that pierces, one shot per pull from a cylinder of 6; it shares its name with the Cardinale enemy.

pages.title: CIMBALO-45
pages.summary: Grade II SMG: 29 damage at 620 rounds a minute on automatic or semi-automatic, a magazine of 25 and a holographic sight.

pages.title: EREMITA .50
pages.summary: Grade IV magnum pistol: 125 damage that pierces two enemies, a magazine of 7 and adjustable iron sights.

pages.title: GLORIA
pages.summary: Grade IV battle rifle: 55 damage at 520 rounds a minute on automatic or semi-automatic, a magazine of 20 and a 4x ACOG.

pages.title: LANCE-7
pages.summary: Grade III precision rifle: 72 damage per semi-automatic shot, a magazine of 12 and a 4x scope.

pages.title: MARTELLO-12
pages.summary: Grade III semi-automatic shotgun: eight pellets of 13 damage per shot, a box magazine of 8 and a red dot.

pages.title: ORIFIAMMA
pages.summary: Grade III bullpup rifle: 32 damage at 680 rounds a minute on automatic or semi-automatic, a magazine of 30 and a 1.5x optic.

pages.title: PIETA' P-9
pages.summary: Grade I pistol and the starting weapon of every game: 25 damage, semi-automatic, a magazine of 15 rounds.

pages.title: PREDICATORE
pages.summary: Grade II lever-action carbine: 66 damage that pierces one more enemy, a tube of 8 rounds reloaded one at a time.

pages.title: PUPILLA
pages.summary: Grade V special weapon, an eye-rifle: a continuous amber beam that pierces everything, 90 damage per shot at 210 rounds a minute, 14 in the magazine.

pages.title: ROSARIO
pages.summary: Grade II bolt-action rifle: 118 damage per shot, a magazine of 5 and a peep sight; the heaviest single hit of its grade.

pages.title: SALTERIO
pages.summary: Grade III drum machine gun: 36 damage at 640 rounds a minute, a drum of 75 rounds and iron sights.

pages.title: SENTINELLA
pages.summary: Grade IV sniper rifle: 190 damage that pierces three enemies, a magazine of 5 and an 8x scope.

pages.title: SERAFINO-18
pages.summary: Grade II machine pistol: 16 damage at 1000 rounds a minute, 20 rounds, with an open red dot.

pages.title: SPORA
pages.summary: Grade IV special weapon, an alien spine launcher of bone and flesh: seven green needles in a fan, a magazine of 6.

pages.title: TARANTOLA
pages.summary: Grade I micro-SMG: 13 damage at 1150 rounds a minute, a magazine of 32 and a peep aperture; a weapon for close range and for spraying.

pages.title: TRINITA'
pages.summary: Grade II burst rifle: 36 damage in three-round bursts, a magazine of 30 and a carry handle with a peep sight.

pages.title: TURIBOLO
pages.summary: Grade III special weapon, a sacred flamethrower: a censer's jet of fire that pierces four enemies at 11 metres, with 120 units of fuel.

pages.title: VESPER-9
pages.summary: Grade II SMG: 20 damage at 850 rounds a minute, a magazine of 40 and a red dot.

pages.title: VIGILIA .45
pages.summary: Grade I pistol: 38 damage per shot with fixed iron sights and a magazine of 8, the hardest hitting pistol of its grade.

pages.title: L'Altare della Consacrazione
pages.summary: Desert-only altar in the presbytery: 40 steel, 5 embers, 3 hearts and 1 relic; it consecrates the weapon in your hand for 3000 points, once per weapon.

pages.title: La Biblioteca dei Voti
pages.summary: Desert-only work in the nave: 30 wood, 30 bones and 2 blood; its lecterns offer three perk books at a time, bought with points.

pages.title: Il Campanile
pages.summary: The bell tower: 40 steel, 30 wood, 5 embers and 1 relic; it brings the return bell, which takes you back up once per expedition.

pages.title: Il Cancello del Conte
pages.summary: The gate of the Count: 60 steel, 5 blood and 1 faith crystal; it needs the sanatorium gate and opens branch IV, Il Guardaroba del Conte.

pages.title: Il Cancello del Sanatorio
pages.summary: The gate of the sanatorium: 45 steel, 30 wood, 3 embers and 1 darkness crystal; it needs the theatre gate and opens branch III.

pages.title: Il Cancello del Teatro
pages.summary: The gate of the theatre: 30 steel, 30 bones and 1 relic; it opens branch II, Il Teatro sepolto.

pages.title: Il Confessionale
pages.summary: Confessional in the west aisle: 25 wood and 4 blood; when you die, your unspent points still give one obolo every 20.

pages.title: Il Rosone
pages.summary: The rose window on the façade, the last work: 3 of each boss resource and 100 each of bones, wood and steel; it consecrates the cathedral and opens the Abyss.

pages.title: Il Tesoro
pages.summary: The treasury in the sacristy: 30 steel, 30 bones and 2 hearts; the points you bring back become oboli at one for every 6, not every 10.

pages.title: La Cappella della Pietra
pages.summary: The chapel of stone on the east aisle: 40 bones, 4 hearts and 2 relics; every expedition starts with the Pelle di pietra perk.

pages.title: La Cappella delle Mani
pages.summary: The chapel of hands on the east aisle: 40 wood, 4 embers and 2 darkness crystals; every expedition starts with the Mani svelte perk.

pages.title: La Fonte battesimale
pages.summary: Baptistery font: 15 bones, 15 steel and 2 blood; from then on every catacomb level starts with at least three holy waters.

pages.title: La Forgia
pages.summary: The forge in the sacristy: 50 steel, 15 wood and 6 embers; +15% damage with every weapon.

pages.title: La Sacrestia
pages.summary: Sacristy: 30 wood and 25 steel; it puts a rack of three free weapons better than the pistol at the start of the expedition.

pages.title: La Vetrata del Cardinale
pages.summary: The Cardinale's window in the nave clerestory: 3 relics and 20 wood; +25% damage to bosses.

pages.title: La Vetrata del Conte
pages.summary: The Count's window in the nave clerestory: 3 gems and 5 blood; perk books cost 40% less.

pages.title: La Vetrata del Direttore
pages.summary: The Direttore's window in the nave clerestory: 3 darkness crystals and 20 steel; area doors cost 25% less.

pages.title: La Vetrata del Primario
pages.summary: The Primario's window in the nave clerestory: 3 faith crystals and 20 bones; +25 maximum health.

pages.title: L'Altare maggiore
pages.summary: High altar: 30 bones, 20 wood and 3 hearts; before each expedition you light one of three candles, which gives a blessing for the whole descent.

pages.title: Le Volte della navata
pages.summary: Nave vaults: 40 wood and 20 steel give the nave its roof back, and every expedition starts with 250 more points.

pages.title: L'Organo
pages.summary: The organ: 50 wood, 30 steel and 4 embers; every wave cleared heals you fully and raises the shield to 100.

pages.title: L'Ossario (the crypt work)
pages.summary: The crypt: 60 bones and 10 wood; from then on, dying keeps every common resource and half of the rare ones.

pages.title: The Abyss
pages.summary: The fifth gate of the standard game, opened by the Rosone: its levels are drawn from the four branches in turn, and its gates lead on down.

pages.title: The catacombs
pages.summary: The standard game's way down: procedural floors in three-level branches, reached through the gates behind the cathedral's apse.

pages.title: The cathedral
pages.summary: Your cathedral, the base of the game: the square and the market outside, the works inside, and the descent behind the apse.
